headline: XDOF in talks for Series B at $1.2B valuation, just 3 months post-stealth
summary: The robotics data startup, founded by UC Berkeley researchers, is rapidly growing and attracting significant VC interest.
details: XDOF, a startup focused on collecting real-world teleoperation data for general-purpose robots, is reportedly in late-stage discussions for a Series B funding round. The deal is expected to value the company at approximately $1.2 billion, led by 8VC.

Emerging from stealth less than three months ago, XDOF has experienced rapid growth, with annualized revenue approaching $50 million. This impressive trajectory has prompted venture capitalists to approach the company for a new funding round, despite it not being planned so soon after its $70 million Series A in June.

Co-founded in 2024 by UC Berkeley researchers Philipp Wu (CEO) and Fred Shentu (CTO), XDOF aims to provide the essential data pipelines, collection tools, and annotation systems that frontier AI and robotics companies often lack the resources to build themselves. This positions XDOF as a critical outsourced data-supply chain for the robotics industry.

The company's foundation lies in research conducted by Wu on GELLO, a low-cost teleoperation system designed to generate training data by allowing remote human control of robotic arms. This work addresses a significant bottleneck in robotics research: the lack of large-scale, real-world datasets comparable to those used for training Large Language Models (LLMs).

XDOF is collaborating with UC Berkeley's AI Research lab to release ABC, which they claim is the largest collection of high-quality robot training data ever assembled. This data is captured through a combination of remote robot teleoperation and human collectors wearing sensors to record everyday tasks.

To scale its operations, XDOF plans to recruit and train data collector teams globally. These teams will include teleoperators who remotely steer robots and egocentric operators who use body sensors to capture movement data, further enhancing the diversity and richness of the training datasets.

headline: Nitter instances increase following previous takedowns
summary: The decentralized Twitter front-end Nitter has seen an increase in active instances, defying earlier efforts to shut them down.
details: Despite previous coordinated efforts to remove Nitter instances, the number of available and working instances has reportedly grown.
Nitter is a privacy-focused alternative front-end for Twitter, allowing users to view tweets without logging in and avoiding Twitter's tracking.
The increase in instances suggests a resilient community effort to maintain access to the service, even in the face of potential legal or technical challenges.
